flags: APA completed its acquisition of Callon Petroleum Company in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $4.5 billion, inclusive of Callon's debt, acquiring approximately 120,000 net acres in the Delaware Basin and 25,000 net acres in the Midland Basin.

APA recorded $1.1 billion of impairments, comprising $796 million of oil and gas property impairments in the North Sea following new regulatory guidelines and obligations in the U.K., a $315 million impairment of U.S. oil and gas properties held-for-sale, and $18 million of inventory impairments.

APA recorded $44 million of impairments, including $18 million of non-operated proved oil and gas property in Egypt, approximately $18 million related to the sale of a U.S. office building, $1 million for GPT facilities in Egypt, and $7 million of inventory impairments in the North Sea.

business_model.claim: APA Corporation is a holding company whose consolidated subsidiaries explore for, develop, and produce crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids (NGLs).
quotes: APA Corporation (APA or the Company) is an independent energy company that owns subsidiaries that explore for, develop, and produce crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs.
As a holding company, APA Corporation’s primary assets are its ownership interests in its consolidated subsidiaries.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and F2
business_model.claim: In addition to selling its own production, APA purchases third-party natural gas and crude oil and resells those volumes to fulfill pipeline takeaway obligations and delivery commitments.
quotes: In order to satisfy certain delivery commitments, the Company purchases third-party natural gas and crude oil to sell and deliver under existing pipeline agreements and sales contracts.
Purchased oil and gas sales represent volumes primarily attributable to domestic gas purchases that were sold by the Company to fulfill natural gas takeaway obligations and delivery commitments.

business_model.claim: APA markets its U.S. crude oil primarily to integrated major oil companies, marketing and transportation companies, and refiners under evergreen and term contracts priced off WTI and Brent-related indices.
quotes: APA primarily markets its U.S. crude oil production to integrated major oil companies, marketing and transportation companies, and refiners based on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) pricing indices (e.g., WTI Houston, West Texas Sour (WTS), WTI Midland, or West Texas Light (WTL) Midland) and some predominately Brent related international pricing indices, adjusted for quality, transportation, and a market-reflective differential.
Sales contracts are generally 30-day evergreen contracts that renew automatically until canceled by either party.

business_model.claim: APA sells U.S. natural gas at monthly or daily liquid index sales points to local distribution, utility, midstream, end-user, marketer, and integrated major oil customers, and sells U.S. NGLs under contracts priced on Gulf Coast market conditions less transportation and fractionation costs or on purchaser weighted-average prices.
quotes: Natural gas is sold to a variety of customers that include local distribution, utility, and midstream companies, as well as end-users, marketers, and integrated major oil companies.

The Company’s U.S. NGL production, which accounted for 98 percent of the Company’s total 2025 NGL production, is sold under contracts with prices at market indices based on Gulf Coast supply and demand conditions, less the costs for transportation and fractionation, or on a weighted-average sales price received by the purchaser.

business_model.claim: Internationally, APA sells substantially all of its Egyptian natural gas production to EGPC under a gas sales agreement, while North Sea natural gas from the Beryl field is processed at the SAGE plant and sold to a third party at St. Fergus on a National Balancing Point index.
quotes: Effective January 2025, substantially all of the Company’s natural gas production was sold to EGPC under the terms of this agreement.
The gas is sold to a third party at the St. Fergus entry point of the national grid on a National Balancing Point index price basis.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: APA organizes and discusses its operations across geographic segments: ongoing production in the U.S., Egypt, and offshore the U.K. in the North Sea, alongside active development in offshore Suriname and exploration interests in Uruguay and Alaska.
quotes: The Company’s business has oil and gas exploration, development, appraisal, and/or ongoing operations primarily in four geographic areas: the U.S., Egypt, offshore the U.K. in the North Sea (North Sea), and offshore Suriname.

APA also has active development, exploration, and appraisal operations ongoing in Suriname, as well as exploration interests in Uruguay, Alaska, and other international locations that may, over time, result in reportable discoveries and development opportunities.

For a more detailed discussion related to the Company’s various geographic segments, refer to “Exploration and Production—Operating Areas” set forth in Part I, Items 1 and 2 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

quotes: The Company’s production revenues and respective contribution to total revenues by country are as follows:

business_model.claim: Crude oil is APA's largest upstream revenue stream, accounting for 80 percent of 2025 oil and gas production revenues ($5,809, table in millions), compared with 11 percent from natural gas ($770) and 9 percent from NGLs ($650).
quotes: Crude oil sales accounted for 80 percent of the Company’s 2025 oil and gas production revenues and 51 percent of its worldwide production.
Natural gas sales accounted for 11 percent of the Company’s 2025 oil and gas production revenues and 32 percent of its worldwide production.
NGL sales accounted for 9 percent of the Company’s 2025 oil and gas production revenues and 17 percent of its worldwide production.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and F2
business_model.claim: APA's Egypt subsidiary under the merged concession agreement is owned by an APA-operated joint venture in which Sinopec holds a minority noncontrolling participation interest, and consolidated revenues, production, and operating expenses include that noncontrolling share.
quotes: The APA subsidiary that is the sole Contractor under the MCA is owned by an APA-operated joint venture owned two-thirds by the Company and one-third by Sinopec International Petroleum Exploration and Production Corporation (Sinopec).
All operating expenses include costs attributable to a noncontrolling interest in Egypt.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: APA's revenues depend heavily on market prices for crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs, which fluctuate with global and domestic supply and demand, OPEC+ actions, geopolitical conflicts, trade policies, and broader economic conditions.
quotes: The Company’s revenues, operating results, future rate of growth, and carrying value of its oil and gas properties depend highly upon the prices it receives for its sales of crude oil, natural gas, and NGL products.
Uncertainties in the global supply chain and financial markets impact oil supply and demand and contribute to commodity price volatility.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: Revenues are also driven by production and sales volumes, which reflect drilling activity and well performance, natural reservoir decline, asset acquisitions and divestitures, operational downtime, voluntary curtailments during weak pricing, and North Sea lifting timing.
quotes: Additionally, the Company has previously and may in the future voluntarily curtail production in response to market conditions, such as weak or negative prices.
Sales volumes may vary from production volumes as a result of the timing of liftings.

business_model.claim: Under Egypt's production-sharing contracts, APA's net entitlement volumes move inversely with commodity prices because cost recovery and EGPC-paid Contractor income taxes are fixed in monetary terms, while those tax payments are grossed up into both revenue and income tax expense with no net economic effect.
quotes: Because Contractor cost recovery entitlement and income taxes paid on its behalf are determined as a monetary amount, the quantities of production entitlement and estimated reserves attributable to these monetary amounts will fluctuate with commodity prices.

In addition, because the Contractor income taxes are paid by EGPC, the amount of the income tax has no economic impact on the Company’s Egypt operations despite impacting the Company’s production and reserves.
Third-quarter 2026 net production was negatively impacted by higher price realizations and lower cost recovery volumes under the production sharing contract.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: Natural gas revenue varies sharply by region due to local pipeline and market conditions, with Permian Basin takeaway constraints depressing U.S. gas realizations while Egypt gas benefits from a contractual price floor with volume upside and North Sea gas tracks U.K. National Balancing Point prices.
quotes: Natural gas, which currently has a limited global transportation system, is subject to price variances based on local supply and demand conditions.

As additional gas pipeline takeaway capacity in the Permian Basin comes online, the spread between Permian and Gulf Coast gas prices may compress, which would reduce the Company’s gain on third-party oil and gas purchases and sales.

business_model.claim: Because APA does not apply hedge accounting to its derivative contracts, changes in derivative fair values flow directly into current-period revenues and other, introducing earnings volatility.
quotes: In addition, because the Company does not apply hedge accounting to its derivative instruments, changes in the fair value of derivatives are recognized in current-period earnings, which may introduce earnings volatility even when the underlying exposure is intended to be economically hedged.

business_model.claim: APA's major operating expenses are depreciation, depletion, and amortization (1,613, table in millions) and lease operating expenses (1,133), followed by general and administrative (295), gathering, processing, transmission and purchased oil and gas costs (282 excluding purchased and 179 for purchased), taxes other than income (184), net financing costs (150), exploration (135), asset retirement obligation accretion (128), and transaction, reorganization, and separation costs (20).

business_model.claim: Lease operating expenses move with commodity-linked field inputs such as power, fuel, and chemicals, service-industry rates for rigs, labor, and marine or helicopter logistics, workover activity, asset mix across oil versus gas and onshore versus offshore, and stock-based compensation allocations.
quotes: Direct operating costs generally trend with commodity prices and are impacted by the type of commodity produced and the location of properties (i.e., offshore, onshore, remote locations, etc.).
Crude oil, which accounted for 51 percent of the Company’s total 2025 production, is inherently more expensive to produce than natural gas.
Lease operating expense guidance has been increased $25 million to $1,525 million to reflect higher stock-based compensation expense allocated to LOE.

business_model.claim: Gathering, processing, and transmission expenses are driven by upstream production volumes and third-party carrier rates, while purchased oil and gas costs vary with domestic gas volumes bought to fulfill delivery commitments and prevailing gas prices at delivery locations.
quotes: GPT costs decreased $8 million compared to 2024, primarily the result of decreased oil production volumes in the U.S. and lower average transportation rates.
The increase is primarily driven by gas volumes purchased at higher prices during 2025 compared to the prior-year period coupled with activity associated with the Callon acquisition.

business_model.claim: DD&A and impairment charges move with production volumes, reserve revisions driven by commodity prices and regulatory changes, and asset sales, while exploration expenses depend on dry hole outcomes, unproved leasehold impairments, and geological and geophysical activity.
quotes: The Company’s oil and gas property DD&A rate remained relatively flat in 2025 compared to 2024, from $13.44 per boe to $13.41 per boe, mainly the result of negative gas price-related reserve revisions in the U.S. Permian Basin offset by non-core asset divestitures.
For example, during 2024, the Company recorded $796 million of impairments for certain of its North Sea proved properties as a result of several new regulatory guidelines and obligations in the U.K.

Exploration expenses include unproved leasehold impairments, exploration dry hole expense, geological and geophysical expenses, and the costs of maintaining and retaining unproved leasehold properties.

business_model.claim: Taxes other than income move primarily with U.S. production revenues through percentage-based severance taxes and ad valorem property taxes, while income tax expense reflects both domestic and foreign taxes and EGPC-paid Egyptian taxes.
quotes: Severance taxes are generally based on a percentage of oil and gas production revenues.
Income taxes paid to the Arab Republic of Egypt on behalf of the Contractor are recognized as oil and gas sales revenue and income tax expense and are reflected as production and estimated reserves.

business_model.basis: stated in P3, P5, and P6
business_model.claim: Company-wide cost-reduction initiatives across overhead, lease operating expenses, and capital spending, alongside substantial debt principal repayments, are lowering APA's recurring cost and interest burden, though share-price increases can raise stock-based compensation expense.
quotes: The Company achieved $350 million in annualized savings across G&A, LOE, and capital as of year-end 2025.
The Company anticipates reaching annualized savings of $500 million by the end of 2026 as a result of these efforts.
Repaid $451 million of debt maturities in the third quarter; total debt has declined by $2.8 billion since year-end 2024, lowering annualized interest expense by more than $180 million;

Focused cost-reduction efforts on personnel and other overhead expenses drove a decrease of $67 million, which more than offset higher stock compensation expense of $45 million primarily driven from an increase in the Company’s stock price during 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, P2, P4, and P6

quotes: If a purchaser of such GOA assets becomes the subject of a case or proceeding under relevant insolvency laws or otherwise fails to perform required abandonment obligations, APA’s subsidiaries could be required to perform such actions under applicable federal laws and regulations.

In addition, after such sources have been exhausted, Apache agreed upon resolution of GOM Shelf’s second bankruptcy to loan GOM Shelf up to $400 million to perform decommissioning, with such loans and related obligations secured by first and prior liens on the Legacy GOA Assets.

competitive_position.claim: APA operates a diversified portfolio spanning U.S. onshore shale and offshore Gulf of America assets, conventional onshore production in Egypt, U.K. North Sea offshore assets, and development in Suriname targeting initial production in 2028.
quotes: APA maintains a diversified asset portfolio, including conventional and unconventional, onshore and offshore, oil and natural gas exploration and production interests, while offering global exploration opportunities.

Internationally, the Company has conventional onshore assets in Egypt’s Western Desert, offshore assets on the U.K.’s Continental Shelf, and is currently progressing with an oil field development offshore Suriname targeting first production in 2028.

APA’s diversified asset portfolio and operational flexibility provide the Company the ability to timely respond to near-term price volatility and effectively manage its investment programs accordingly.
